notes: Built from the PDF only; the download holds one clean copy of the guideline (no redline), 8 pages, Reviewed 06/25/26, Revised 07/15/26, Original Effective Date 01/01/01. effective_date is the Revised date and reviewed_date the Reviewed date, following the hand-built example; the original effective date (01/01/01) is not recorded as effective_date.

Two pathways: primary heart/lung transplantation and retransplantation after a failed primary heart/lung transplant. Retransplantation 'meets the definition of medical necessity in individuals who meet criteria for heart/lung transplantation', so the retransplant pathway is the full primary tree plus one extra leaf, a failed primary heart/lung transplant.

Code-to-pathway mapping: the document ties no code to any section. All three codes (33930 donor cardiectomy-pneumonectomy, 33933 backbench preparation of the donor heart/lung allograft, 33935 heart-lung transplant with recipient cardiectomy-pneumonectomy) are components of one heart/lung transplant, and the document never says a code is non-covered or investigational, so all three are tagged covered and both pathways list all three explicitly. Primary and retransplant are distinguished by history, not by code.

Each indication bullet 'X with heart failure' is split into a diagnosis leaf and a heart-failure leaf joined by all (a chart can document the lung diagnosis without the heart failure). 'severe heart failure' (bullets 2, 4, 6) and 'heart failure' (bullets 1, 3, 5, 7) are kept as two criteria because severity is a distinct thing a chart documents. Bullet 7, 'Pulmonary fibrosis with uncontrollable pulmonary hypertension or heart failure', is all(pulmonary fibrosis, any(uncontrollable pulmonary hypertension, heart failure)). Bullet 3 'Eisenmenger complex with irreversible pulmonary hypertension and heart failure' is all of three leaves; 'irreversible pulmonary hypertension' there is kept separate from bullet 1's 'Irreversible primary pulmonary hypertension' because one is secondary to the congenital shunt and the other primary/idiopathic. A reviewer could instead keep each bullet as one leaf; the verdict is the same either way.

'Non-specific severe pulmonary fibrosis' (bullet 2) and 'Pulmonary fibrosis' (bullet 7) are separate leaves as written; a chart with severe pulmonary fibrosis and heart failure satisfies bullet 7 in any case.

The indication list is introduced with 'including, but not limited to, one of the following conditions'. A program cannot evaluate an open-ended list, so the tree requires one of the seven listed conditions in addition to end-stage cardiac and pulmonary disease; a reviewer could accept an unlisted end-stage cardiopulmonary condition under 'not limited to', but the next sentence makes all other situations experimental or investigational, so the listed conditions are treated as the coverable set.
'carefully selected individuals' is not modelled: it is not a requirement a chart could document separately from the listed criteria.

The contraindication list is headed 'Potential contraindications to heart/lung transplant (subject to the judgment of the transplant center) include'. Modelled as not(any(the seven bullets)) inside each pathway's all, so a documented contraindication fails the pathway; the 'potential' and 'subject to the judgment of the transplant center' wording means a reviewer could treat a documented contraindication as a review item rather than a hard fail. Not listed under exclusions because they are conditional on center judgment rather than categorical non-coverage statements.
The Certificate of Medical Necessity block (submit a completed CMN with the request) is an administrative submission step, not a clinical requirement, and is left out of the tree.
No ICD-10 codes are listed in the Billing/Coding section (the 2010 update history mentions related ICD-10 codes, but none are printed), so scope.icd10 is empty.

Program exceptions: FEP and SAO follow their own guidelines; for Medicare Advantage the document says NCD 260.9 Heart Transplants 'was reviewed on the last guideline reviewed date', which is read as Medicare Advantage following the NCD rather than this guideline, so it is listed under excluded_plans. The step-therapy exemption paragraph is boilerplate (this guideline has no step therapy requirement) and is left out.

The Description section (evidence summary: UpToDate, ISHLT guidelines, registry survival studies, HIV and pretransplant malignancy studies) is background and holds no requirements; nothing from it is in the tree. The 'Other' section quotes Florida statutes on non-discrimination in transplant coverage and is likewise left out.

Related guidelines (Lung and Lobar Lung Transplant 02-30000-10, Heart Transplant 02-33000-23, Total Artificial Hearts and VADs 02-33000-25) govern isolated lung or heart transplant and VADs, not the combined heart/lung procedure, and are not part of this tree.
